tools.name: score_buying_signal_evidence
tools.description: Deterministically score caller-supplied business-account fit and buying-signal evidence. Returns a review-only scorecard, evidence gaps, and unsupported-claim flags. The tool does not fetch sources, access Intakra workspaces, store input, spend money, draft outreach, or send anything.

tools.name: prepare_why_now_review
tools.description: Turn caller-supplied fit criteria and business signals into reviewable why-now and fit guidance. Every fact remains labeled caller-supplied and unverified. The tool does not research, infer budget or buyer intent as fact, draft outreach, access private data, persist input, or take action.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Use for 'which companies am I tracking?' or 'is acme.com on my list?'. Lists the accounts (companies) on the connected workspace's list, or matches domains you pass against it, with each account's last recorded check date, the domains not on the list and pagination. Saved records only: adds nothing

tools.name: prioritize_accounts
tools.description: Use for 'who should I target from my list?' or 'are these companies showing buying signals?'. Ranks tracked accounts by their best open lead for what you sell (and by the account score for fit, timing and reach, 0 to 100, when it is on for the workspace), each with dated proof, links and a rough tim

tools.name: get_account_changes
tools.description: Use for 'anything happening on my list?' or 'what changed at these companies this week?'. Returns findings recorded since a date (default seven days ago) for the tracked accounts, each with the event date, the date Intakra recorded it and a source link. Optional domains restrict the list. tools.name: list_opportunities
tools.description: Use for 'which accounts have an open buying signal?'. Returns open leads (id eop_..., dated proof with links, what it usually means for what you sell, rough time frame); filter closing_soon returns the ones that usually wind down within 30 days. Use the returned id with get_best_contact, get_project

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Use for 'what do we know about acme.com?'. Returns one tracked account: up to 12 recent dated findings with links, and its open leads with dated proof. Pass a domain (acme.com), a company name or an account id. Saved records only, no new check.

tools.name: get_project_updates
tools.description: Use when the user asks what changed on one lead. Pass opportunity_id from list_opportunities or get_daily_brief (eop_...). Returns whether the lead is watched and up to 20 dated before/after changes with sources. Saved evidence only: no new research and no notification.

tools.name: add_accounts
tools.description: Use after the user asks to add companies. Adds accounts to the list by website domain (for example ["acme.com", "globex.com"]). Domains already on the list are skipped and the plan's account limit applies. Checks of new accounts start in the normal background pass, subject to the plan; this returns

tools.name: get_offering
tools.description: Use before set_offering, or for 'what does Intakra think we sell?'. Returns the workspace's current description of what it sells, exactly as stored, or null when none is on file. Intakra uses it to decide which findings become leads. Read only.

tools.name: set_offering
tools.description: Use only after the user confirms the new text; call get_offering first to show what it replaces. Replaces what the workspace sells, in a sentence or two (for example "Payroll software for restaurant groups with 5 to 50 locations"). Intakra uses it to decide which findings become leads. tools.name: get_daily_brief
tools.description: Use for 'what should I look at today?' or 'who is worth a call?'. Returns the leads in today's note: for each, what we found (dated, with links), what it usually means for what you sell, who to reach and why, and roughly how much time there is. If no note went out yet today, returns what the next on

tools.name: get_best_contact
tools.description: Use for 'who should I reach about this lead, and why?'. Pass a lead id (eop_... or a match of your own rule) from list_opportunities or get_daily_brief. Returns the person who most likely owns it and why: name, role, LinkedIn, and a verified work email when there is one (never for EU, EEA or UK comp

tools.name: list_suggestions
tools.description: Use for 'which accounts did Intakra suggest?'. Returns companies Intakra suggested adding to the list (from filings, news and lookalikes of your customers), each with the reason. Suggestions do not count toward the plan until approved in Intakra.

tools.name: request_accounts
tools.description: Use when the user asks Intakra to find companies, and ask first. Requests account suggestions from a short description, an industry, a size range, a country, or up to 5 customer domains. Runs in the background; results arrive later as suggestions (list_suggestions) and never count toward the plan un

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_project_updates, get_best_contact · Private data: prepare_why_now_review, list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account_changes, list_opportunities, get_account, get_offering, get_daily_brief, get_best_contact · Public sink: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_best_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_project_updates, get_best_contact · Private data: prepare_why_now_review, list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account_changes, list_opportunities, get_account, get_offering, get_daily_brief, get_best_contact · Public sink: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_best_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
